newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower, but golds restrain fall.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower, but golds restrain fall.

text.p: Toronto stocks snapped a three-day winning streak on Friday, but shining golds restrained the fall on Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index dropped 49.92 points, or 0.72 percent, to close at 6895.15. The key index earlier sank more than one percent, but recovered in later trading.
Nearly 85 million shares were traded worth C$1.4 billion ($1 billion).

"We've been pretty rich these last couple of months and now we're seeing a bit of a correction," one Toronto stock trader said. A buoyant gold price helped Canadian equities avoid matching a 156-point drop in the Dow Jones average.
The gold and precious metals index jumped 263 points, or 3.2 percent, as COMEX gold futures rallied on a weak U.S. dollar, bonds and stocks. COMEX October gold ended up $4.60 at $328.30 an ounce.
